judge.notes:
I checked the BRD statement by statement against the five inputs (feat.fitment, feat.intake, org.templates, org.strategy_capability, org.decision_log). I also checked it against feat.classification, feat.prebacklog, requirements/ZD-48600.md, COMMUNICATION.md and the brief.

What is supported:
- All eight BRD template sections (problem, business outcome, users, scope, out of scope, business rules, success measures, approvals) are present, plus a business question set and a validation check. The workbook action is covered.
- Every number traces to a cited source:
  - 30 and 10, the > thresholds, and "two decimals" come from feat.intake CR-3, CR-5 and CR-6.
  - The bucket ranges come from org.strategy_capability.
  - T2, R-AP-12/14, Q4 2026, REG-LPR-2026-4.2 at 60 days, PROV-ACME-2026-11 and 2026-12-01 come from feat.fitment.
  - 2026-10-24 comes from feat.intake.
  - Feed v2 and v3 come from feat.fitment and feat.intake.
  - D-2026-031, D-2026-044 and D-2026-050 come from org.decision_log. L-007 and L-011 come from memory.
  - Node.js comes from ZD-48600.md.
- The boundary derivations (exactly 30 days is not listed; a delay of exactly 30 is medium; exactly 10 is low) follow directly from the strict > rules and from feat.prebacklog.
- The row classes and columns match the design-library override in ZD-48600.md. "PM and Leadership approved REQ-03" matches COMMUNICATION.md.
- The assumptions B-A1 to B-A7 trace correctly to feat.fitment FQ-1 and feat.prebacklog A-1 to A-5. The open-question owners are carried over faithfully.
- OQ-B7 correctly notes that org.templates holds no business question set, although the brief says it does.
- The decision-log check (no conflict) is accurate.

The previous refusal point is not properly fixed. SM-5 now quotes the architecture rule correctly, but it says CR-4 is the only change to an existing function. That contradicts feat.classification, which it cites, and the BRD's own section 4 and OS-6, all of which name CR-1 (feed ingestion, new paid_date column and reject reason) as a second change to existing behaviour.

Two smaller issues: "delivers R-AP-12" overstates the fitment's "matches", and the auditability-support claim is not labelled as agent judgement. Neither changes the substance. The SM-5 contradiction should be fixed before the Leadership gate.
